rollups.text: James Perez’s real-estate investment plan developed from initial interest to active property evaluation. On 2024-03-15, James was a beginner based in North Ericshire, Turkey, seeking security and steady income and favoring residential rentals; he discussed saving, a $50,000 initial-capital allocation, and a 7% annual rental-yield goal. He considered single-family and multifamily properties, Istanbul and North Ericshire locations, financing, and a course beginning 2024-03-20. By 2024-04-10, after evaluating an Ataturk Street property whose modeled returns varied substantially with assumptions and were sometimes far below his target, James leaned toward small multifamily properties and continued comparing neighborhoods and listings. On 2024-04-10, he also reported Halkbank pre-approval for $80,000 at 9.5% APR, valid for 90 days. On 2024-04-14, he planned an inspection with contractor Cem Yildiz; by 2024-04-20, he intended to decide whether to accept the Ataturk Street asking price, negotiate, or walk away. The records do not establish that he purchased a property or completed the planned steps.

James Perez’s Ataturk Street property evaluation progressed through changing estimates and a planned purchase decision. On 2024-04-10, James discussed a $95,000 property, estimated repairs of $3,200, and projected rents that varied across scenarios; assistant calculations using different assumptions ranged from negative returns to estimates near or above James’s 7% target. James planned to inspect the property with Cem Yildiz on 2024-04-14, focusing on roof and plumbing, and to review the report, repair estimates, comparable properties, total costs, and projected cash flow before deciding by 2024-04-20 whether to accept, negotiate, or walk away. James later said the low modeled returns were unacceptable and considered other properties and further negotiation. No final offer, acceptance, or purchase is recorded; assistant-generated rent, expense, and ROI calculations were illustrative and inconsistent across scenarios.

James Perez’s property-type preference shifted as he compared expected yield, cost, and management burden. On 2024-03-15, he considered a $75,000 single-family home projected at 6% yield and a $110,000 duplex projected at 8%; he expressed interest in the duplex’s higher yield and diversification, while also asking about starting small and managing complexity. Assistant advice varied, including a recommendation to start with the single-family home and conditional support for the duplex. On 2024-04-10, after the Ataturk Street scenario appeared unlikely to meet his 7% target, James said he favored multifamily properties and chose to pursue viewings of smaller multifamily units, while acknowledging their higher upfront cost and management complexity. No purchase is recorded.

James Perez planned a mortgage pre-approval process with an April 15, 2024 deadline. On 2024-03-15, he was worried about missing the deadline; assistant-proposed steps included gathering documents, comparing lenders, applying, responding to requests, and reviewing a final letter. On 2024-04-10, James reported that Halkbank had pre-approved him for $80,000 at 9.5% APR for 90 days. The records do not establish the loan term or that he accepted or drew the mortgage.

James Perez explored professional property management while considering a rental investment. He met property manager Manuel at the North Ericshire Investors Meetup on 2024-03-05 and later asked about local management companies and software. He interviewed Selin Kaya on 2024-04-09; she was described as having seven years of experience. On 2024-04-10, James planned to request her fee details, references, contract terms, and emergency-response approach, and to seek comparison quotes from other managers. He said he would weigh a manager’s time savings and expertise against a lower ROI. Proposed emails and follow-up meetings are recorded, but no confirmed hiring or completed contact is established.

Property-search platforms James Perez used, considered, or planned to use: Sahibinden.com, considered by 2024-03-15 and used in property research (2024-03-15; T118, T128); Emlakjet.com, used since 2024-04-05 after Manuel recommended it, and planned for searches, alerts, and neighborhood data gathering on 2024-04-10 (2024-04-05; 2024-04-10; T294, T296, T310, T312). James considered Emlakjet.com and Sahibinden.com strong platforms and said he would probably stick with Emlakjet.com, while also planning to collect data from both for comparisons on 2024-04-10 (T308, T320, T322).

People involved in James Perez’s real-estate planning: Amanda, James’s mentor and friend, met at the North Ericshire Psychology Conference on 2010-06-12; James planned to discuss investment plans with her on 2024-03-15, while her real-estate expertise remained uncertain (T36, T46). Randy, a friend James met at the North Ericshire Book Club on 2012-01-20, has discussed investments with him; James trusted his opinion and planned to ask him to review his investment budget on 2024-03-15 (T58, T62). Mehmet Yilmaz, a local agent James said had 15 years of experience, had viewings scheduled with James for 2024-03-25 and 2024-03-27; James also planned further property discussions and viewings in April 2024 (T132, T138, T278, T339). Manuel shared property-management information at the North Ericshire Investors Meetup on 2024-03-05 and recommended Emlakjet.com (T186, T294). Selin Kaya, described as having seven years’ property-management experience, was interviewed by James on 2024-04-09; James considered her as a potential manager (T332, T352). Cem Yildiz was scheduled to inspect a property with James on 2024-04-14 (T378, T390).

James Perez asked about or compared rental-property options repeatedly: on 2024-03-15 he considered single-family versus multifamily investments in North Ericshire in several separate discussions, including management, maintenance, costs, and remote oversight; on 2024-04-10 he compared Ataturk and Cumhuriyet neighborhoods and shifted toward small multifamily properties. The records document multiple discussions, not a count of completed purchases.

James Perez’s stated initial-capital figures changed or differed across discussions: on 2024-03-15, he said he had set aside $50,000 (T50, T68); later that date he said he increased his allocation to $60,000 (T242). On 2024-04-10, he again described an initial-capital allocation of $50,000 (T250, T251). These are reported figures at different points, not evidence that the amounts were cumulative or that a purchase occurred.

James Perez repeatedly identified a 7% annual rental-yield goal: first stated as a target by 2024-12-01 on 2024-03-15, reiterated on 2024-04-10, and used to assess candidate properties. On 2024-04-10, he concluded that the Ataturk Street property’s modeled returns were too low in some scenarios and favored seeking higher-rental-potential or multifamily properties. The assistant’s calculations depended on varying, often illustrative assumptions and were not verified property results.

James Perez’s planned or scheduled property-related appointments: property viewings with agent Mehmet Yilmaz on 2024-03-25 and 2024-03-27 (T138); a viewing meeting with Mehmet Yilmaz scheduled for 2024-04-12 at 3:00 PM, with questions and documents to prepare (source record has no source ID); a planned Ataturk Street viewing around 2024-04-10, for which James intended to contact Mehmet to confirm logistics (T278, T280); and a home inspection with contractor Cem Yildiz scheduled for 2024-04-14 at 10:00 AM, with James planning to attend and obtain a detailed report (T378, T390, T392). These records establish plans or appointments, not that each meeting occurred.

James Perez’s Ataturk Street property evaluation and proposed purchase progressed from considering a $95,000 property and its below-target return on 2024-04-10, through repair-based negotiation planning on 2024-05-05, to an amended contract received on 2024-05-03 and a mortgage he said was finalized on 2024-05-05. A May 23 walkthrough and May 25 closing were scheduled or discussed, while roof and plumbing work was scheduled for May 26–June 10. These records describe plans and scheduled steps; they do not confirm that closing, repairs, or move-in were completed. The key milestones span 56 days from April 10 to June 5, with repair work scheduled to continue through June 10.
rollups.topic: Ataturk Street property purchase and renovation

rollups.text: On 2024-04-10, James Perez was nervous about a first lawyer review of a real-estate purchase contract scheduled for 2024-04-22 at 11:00 AM. He planned to send the contract to his lawyer, reread it, highlight unclear clauses, bring supporting documents, and prepare questions about price, repairs, fees, maintenance, warranties, resale restrictions, laws, and taxes. On 2024-05-03, he received a contract with minor amendments including a seller’s repair warranty, and on 2024-05-05 asked how to review it and whether to coordinate with the seller, lawyer, or both. The records do not confirm what happened at the April 22 meeting or whether the amended contract was subsequently approved.

On 2024-05-05, James Perez said tenant screening had been postponed until 2024-06-15 and was weighing whether to wait or accelerate it. He felt overwhelmed by contract review and screening, worried about tenant quality, and repeatedly considered contacting prospective tenants to build a backup list. Advice included promptly marketing the property, prequalifying applicants, using consistent screening criteria and a screening service, and balancing tenant quality with occupancy speed. No outreach, screening, tenant selection, or incentive offer is confirmed.

On 2024-05-05, James Perez was considering property manager Selin Kaya’s proposed 9% monthly fee, which he understood to be within the 8–10% range discussed in a webinar. He considered it reasonable but planned to ask whether it could be reduced to 8.5% or 8%, request a detailed list of included services, and obtain competing quotes. He intended to document any agreement in writing. No negotiation outcome, service list, or management agreement is recorded.

James Perez compared liability insurance options from Allianz and Anadolu Sigorta on 2024-04-10, leaning toward the less expensive option but not wanting to sacrifice coverage. On 2024-05-05, he said he had chosen Allianz liability insurance for his investment property at $450 per year. The conversation does not establish the policy’s limits, deductible, exclusions, or whether it was ultimately bound; he was advised to verify those terms and rental-specific protections.

James Perez’s financing and refinancing discussions developed from concern about a 9.5% APR on a Halkbank pre-approval on 2024-05-05 to saying that his Halkbank mortgage was finalized later that day. He described a fixed 9.5% APR, $72,000 principal, and 10-year term; payment and total-interest figures in the conversation were assistant estimates. He also explored refinancing after three years, including rate changes, fees, break-even time, appraisal and appreciation risk, and protection against rates rising before refinancing. No refinance application or decision to refinance is confirmed.

James Perez said on 2024-05-01 that renovation stress had led him to resume weekly yoga classes. On 2024-05-05, he said he still felt overwhelmed by renovation and investment decisions. Earlier, on 2024-04-10, he described wanting to avoid overwork and planned to finish urgent investment tasks before a hiking break, possibly delegate responsibilities, enjoy the hikes, and journal. The April 15–16 North Ericshire National Park itinerary was assistant-suggested and was not independently confirmed as completed.

On 2024-05-05, James Perez expressed concern that 2024 fire-safety regulations could add costs to his rental-property investment. He asked about applicable requirements, equipment maintenance, and whether extinguisher use required specific certification. Advice was to verify requirements with local authorities and building or fire officials, identify applicable rules before budgeting, and keep compliance records. No specific requirement or certification applicable to his property was established. On 2024-05-27, he said he had scheduled smoke-detector installation for that date; the record does not confirm installation was completed.
entities: North Ericshire fire and building authorities

rollups.text: Real-estate property types James Perez considered or discussed: a single-family home on Ataturk Street (discussed at $95,000 on 2024-04-10 and again in May; no purchase completion confirmed); a multi-family property on Cumhuriyet Street, including a two-unit comparison on 2024-05-05; and a $105,000 duplex offer, which James said he declined on 2024-05-01. James said he preferred starting with single-family homes and potentially considering multi-family properties later.

People who recurred in James Perez’s real-estate discussions: Amanda, who advised him about insurance priorities and tenant maintenance clauses (2024-04-10 and 2024-05-04..2024-05-05); Randy, who discussed investment strategy with James and reviewed his investment spreadsheet (2024-04-10 and 2024-05-02); Cem Yildiz, the contractor associated with inspection, repairs, and renovation plans (2024-04-10..2024-06-10); Mehmet, the real-estate agent involved in a scheduled walkthrough and closing discussions (2024-05-23); and Selin Kaya, a property manager whose proposed fee James considered (2024-05-05).

Property repair, upgrade, and furnishing activities discussed for James Perez’s potential rental property: roof and plumbing repairs (estimates discussed 2024-04-10 and work scheduled for 2024-05-26..2024-06-10); an additional electrical-repair estimate (2024-04-10 and 2024-05-05); repainting in neutral tones and LED lighting (planned by 2024-05-05); and furniture selection and delivery planning, including a $1,000 furnishing budget discussed on 2024-05-05 and a delivery scheduled for 2024-05-28. These records include plans, examples, and scheduled work, not confirmation that all work or delivery occurred.

James Perez discussed the property manager Selin Kaya’s 9% monthly fee in multiple records on 2024-05-05. He initially described it as reasonable because it fell within an 8–10% range, while also planning to seek a reduction to 8.5% or 8%, request service details, and compare other managers. This reflects a qualified acceptance of the stated range alongside a plan to negotiate, not a confirmed fee change.

James Perez repeatedly expressed a preference for single-family homes as his initial investment approach, citing simpler management and limited capital, while keeping open the possibility of multi-family investment later. This preference was stated on 2024-04-10 and revisited on 2024-05-05; it is not a rejection of multi-family properties for the future.

James Perez discussed tenant-screening postponement and occupancy trade-offs repeatedly on 2024-05-05: he cited screening postponed until 2024-06-15, weighed tenant quality against faster occupancy, and considered building a backup applicant list. The records establish repeated consideration and concern, not completed outreach or screening.

James Perez’s real-estate focus shifted from single-family rentals toward multifamily investing. On 2024-05-05 he asked about single-family versus multifamily properties and was told single-family homes are generally easier to self-manage (T872–T875). On 2024-06-15 he reaffirmed a preference for single-family homes under $100,000 with 6–7% yields, while also considering multifamily properties in nearby towns (T946–T949; T1062–T1063). By 2024-06-15 he had decided to diversify into multifamily properties by Q4 2024 (T1082). On 2024-08-01 he said he had decided to invest in a four-unit Yenişehir property priced at $130,000, with a projected 9% yield; this records a decision, not a completed purchase (T1180–T1181; T1224–T1225).

James Perez’s evaluation of a four-unit multifamily property in Yenişehir progressed from considering the opportunity to deciding to invest. On 2024-08-01, Mehmet introduced him to the $130,000 property, described as having a projected 9% yield ($11,700 annual gross rent); James also said he had $60,000 available and weighed Manuel’s advice to keep renovations under $12,000 against a possible $15,000 budget (T1180–T1181; T1210–T1214). That same day James said he had decided to invest, and the proposed next steps included financing, inspection, title and zoning checks, legal review, renovation planning, and property management; no completed purchase was reported (T1224–T1227). A viewing with Mehmet and contractor Cem was scheduled for 2024-08-05, four days after the decision, with James intending to assess unit condition, renovation costs, rental demand, expenses, zoning, and projected cash flow (T1246; T1276–T1278).
rollups.topic: Yenişehir four-unit property evaluation and investment decision

rollups.text: James Perez’s Buildium use developed from exploring automation to reporting that he had begun using the software. On 2024-06-15, he asked how rent reminders work and said Manuel had helped him with Buildium; the suggested setup included reminder timing, communication methods, recipients, and delivery monitoring (T1006–T1009). Later that day he said he would follow suggested setup steps, but did not confirm completion then (T1021–T1023). On 2024-08-01, he said he had started using Buildium to track rent and manage maintenance requests. He considered QuickBooks, Trello, and First Advantage but had not reported adopting or integrating them (T1202–T1205).

James Perez planned a summer garden redesign to improve curb appeal, with an $800 budget and an 2024-08-01 target. By 2024-08-01 he had not selected a landscape contractor and asked how to find a reliable one; the conversation gives no confirmation that the redesign was completed. The planning period from the June 2024 discussions to the target date was approximately six weeks, and the contractor search was still unresolved on the target date.

Smart-home devices James Perez installed, selected, or planned for his property: Nest thermostat, installed 2024-06-10; Philips Hue smart lights and August Smart Lock, selected by 2024-06-15, with installation planned for July 2024. The records confirm the thermostat installation and selection/plans for the other devices, not their installation.

Property-management and renovation people discussed in multiple records: Selin Kaya, property manager, discussed for day-to-day operations and management fees on 2024-06-15 and again as a prospective manager for the Yenişehir property on 2024-08-01; Cem, contractor, discussed regarding repair work and coordination on 2024-06-15 and scheduled to attend a property viewing with James Perez and Mehmet on 2024-08-05; Manuel, who helped James Perez with Buildium by 2024-06-15 and advised on renovation budgeting on 2024-08-01; and Mehmet, who introduced James Perez to the Yenişehir property on 2024-08-01 and was scheduled to attend the viewing on 2024-08-05.

James Perez’s stated property-investment preference evolved across at least three recorded stages: on 2024-06-15 he reaffirmed a focus on single-family homes under $100,000 with 6–7% yields; by 2024-06-15 he had decided to diversify into multifamily properties by Q4 2024; and on 2024-08-01 he said he had decided to invest in a specific four-unit Yenişehir property. The last record is a decision, not proof of a completed purchase.

James Perez’s Yenişehir four-unit property investment progressed from evaluating the $130,000 property and its rental potential on 2024-08-01 to financing and renovation planning in September. On 2024-08-01 he considered a seven-year hold, a $15,000 renovation, professional management, and a $60,000 funding scenario; these were considerations and illustrative assumptions, not proof of purchase. Ziraat Bank approved a $100,000 mortgage on 2024-09-15. On 2024-09-20 James said the purchase price was $130,000, with $12,000 renovation and $1,500 furnishing costs; a closing was scheduled for 2024-09-28. The assistant’s cash-flow and return estimates varied substantially between scenarios and were not verified results. Elapsed time from initial evaluation to reported loan approval: 45 days; from evaluation to scheduled closing: 58 days.

James Perez’s renovation planning for the Yenişehir property developed from considering repairs and upgrades on 2024-08-01 to a reported renovation kickoff on 2024-09-20. Early discussions considered a $15,000 renovation and phased work; on 2024-09-20 James prioritized essential repairs, functional improvements, kitchen and bathroom upgrades, then paint and flooring. Contractor Cem’s unexpected plumbing issue delayed the start by three days and put the October 31 completion deadline at risk. Cem requested an additional $1,200 for plumbing, which James decided to add to the renovation budget and reallocate from furnishings. The budget discussion therefore moved from $12,000 to $13,200; James also stated that he had not approved other additional expenses or reallocations. He chose to decline a seller’s $5,000 early buyout offer and keep the renovation schedule rather than rush work. Elapsed time from early renovation planning to reported kickoff: about 50 days.

James Perez planned for Selin to manage parts of the Yenişehir rental operation. On 2024-08-01 he weighed the time savings and expertise against a 10% management fee, and also considered self-management with selective outsourcing. By 2024-09-20 he considered hiring Selin, noting her seven years of complex-property experience, and planned a clear contract and regular updates. He also planned to train another person on basic tasks and document property records and vendor contacts to reduce dependence on Selin. On 2024-09-20 he assigned Selin property marketing and tenant screening for a target occupancy date of 2024-10-15, and planned weekly meetings and monthly marketing reports. The record establishes plans and assignments, not whether Selin ultimately began or completed the work.

James Perez tracked environmental due diligence for the Yenişehir property. On 2024-08-01 a report was described as ordered and expected by August 14; later conversation described a report dated August 12 that found no significant environmental concerns and required no additional mitigation. James said the clean report was a relief and planned to focus on financing and contractors. The report details and clean findings were provided in assistant responses; the record does not independently verify the report. Elapsed time from the stated order date to the report’s stated date: 11 days.

James Perez’s renovation safety-inspection discussion moved from a scheduled mid-renovation inspection on 2024-10-05 to a later account that an inspection took place on 2024-10-04. The reported findings were improperly installed electrical wiring, blocked fire exits, and minor structural issues. The conversation says a licensed electrician repaired the wiring and issued a compliance certificate, exits were cleared and markings updated, and structural repairs were completed with an engineer’s report. A municipal follow-up inspection was reported scheduled for 2024-10-15; no result is provided. James requested that renovation-progress updates always confirm whether inspections were completed and report their results. The chronology includes conflicting descriptions of the inspection date and does not establish a follow-up result.

James Perez considered how Yenişehir’s public transit line could affect investment performance. Before its opening, August 2024 discussions treated transit as a possible source of higher demand, rents, occupancy, and appreciation. The line was reported to have opened on 2024-09-15. On 2024-09-20 James agreed improved access could attract tenants and planned to highlight the line in marketing, update listings and brochures, and consider bike storage and waiting areas. These are anticipated effects and planned marketing actions; no realized rent or value impact is reported. Elapsed time from opening to discussion: 5 days.

James Perez discussed a possible refinancing exit for a property. On 2024-09-20 he said he planned to refinance after two years if the property appreciated by 12%, and reaffirmed that plan. He intended to track value and market conditions, maintain credit and financial stability, and obtain a recent appraisal before deciding whether to hold, convert to a short-term rental, or sell. The 12% appreciation is a target or assumption, not an achieved result, and no later appraisal outcome is recorded.

James Perez’s recurring real-estate discussions concerned these properties and opportunities: Ataturk Street single-family home, discussed by 2024-05-05 with a $95,000 asking price, $650 rent estimate, and $90,000 offer; a four-unit Yenişehir property, evaluated from 2024-08-01 and discussed in financing, renovation, and management contexts through 2024-09-20; and an unspecified property viewing planned for 2024-08-05. The Ataturk Street figures and Yenişehir estimates are conversation details, not confirmation that either purchase was completed.

People repeatedly involved in James Perez’s real-estate discussions: Mehmet, his lawyer and a contact who introduced the Yenişehir multifamily opportunity; Cem, the renovation contractor; Selin, considered and later assigned property-management and tenant-marketing work; Randy, whom James met at The Green Olive for investment and renovation discussions; Amanda, James’s investment mentor whom he said he usually consults weekly; and Susan, who was involved in renovation coordination discussions. The records do not establish that every proposed meeting, contract, or work assignment was completed.

Renovation materials and upgrades James Perez discussed or selected: on 2024-08-01 he expressed preferences for locally sourced, recycled, durable, low-maintenance, non-toxic and low-VOC materials, and planned to contact suppliers for reclaimed wood, recycled glass, low-VOC paint, and insulation. On 2024-09-20 he planned bamboo flooring, low-VOC paint, LED lighting, and possibly smart lighting; he specifically preferred zero-VOC Benjamin Moore Natura paint. He also said he had selected eco-friendly paint and LED lighting for all units with a $2,000 budget, intending to prioritize visible areas and possibly phase the rest. The records describe choices and plans, not confirmed installation.

James Perez’s recurring property-management and tenant priorities included tenant screening, retention, marketing, and safety. On 2024-08-01 he asked about screening and emergency preparedness, and favored safety measures such as drills and signage. On 2024-09-20 he assigned Selin marketing and screening for a 2024-10-15 occupancy target, planned to focus on retention and increase marketing, and discussed emergency safety and compliance. These were plans and discussion points; later occupancy or implementation results are not recorded.

James Perez described several stress-management practices during renovation. On 2024-08-01 he planned a retreat at Lake Sapanca from August 10 through August 12, with nature walks and possible swimming. On 2024-09-20 he said renovation stress had led him to increase meditation to twice daily and planned to continue, possibly trying guided meditation; he also discussed keeping a consistent routine and taking short breaks. He later said he felt overwhelmed and was unsure whether meditation was helping. The retreat is recorded as planned, not confirmed as completed.

James Perez’s discussed renovation budget changed from $12,000 to $13,200 after contractor Cem requested $1,200 for plumbing repairs on 2024-09-20. James said he would fund the increase by reallocating furnishing money. He separately stated he had not approved any other additional renovation expenses or budget reallocations. Thus, one $1,200 increase is explicitly approved in the records; other proposed allocations remain examples or suggestions.

James Perez’s position on professional management shifted from weighing Selin’s 10% fee against self-management on 2024-08-01, to considering Selin’s experience on 2024-09-20, and then assigning her marketing and tenant-screening tasks. He also planned to reduce dependency by training another person and documenting vendors and property records. This records a change from considering self-management to delegating specific duties; it does not establish that he signed a full-service management contract.

James Perez discussed at least two distinct property viewing plans: an unspecified property viewing scheduled for 2024-08-05, for which he planned to review listing information and bring measuring and note-taking tools; and a Yenişehir property viewing also described as scheduled for August 5, whose completion was not confirmed. A later 2024-09-20 record refers to the Yenişehir viewing date as already past and says its year was unspecified. The records do not establish how many viewings actually occurred.

James Perez’s real-estate holdings and prospective acquisitions: Atatürk Street single-family property (listed at $95,000 with $650 monthly rent; James offered $90,000 on 2024-05-05; later described as purchased on 2024-05-25, with tenants from 2024-07-01, though some details appear only in assistant statements); Yenişehir multifamily property (considered in 2024, with purchase and renovation details later asserted by the assistant but not consistently confirmed by James); a $120,000 North Ericshire duplex (James said on 2025-01-15 he would proceed, but completion is not recorded); and a Cumhuriyet Avenue property advertised at $95,000 and 7% yield (James expressed intent to proceed on 2025-01-15, but completion is not recorded). James also considered properties on Atatürk Street, in Yenişehir, and other areas for future acquisitions.

James Perez’s recorded real-estate investment actions: he offered $90,000 for the Atatürk Street property on 2024-05-05; completed a garden redesign there for $850 on 2024-11-08; rejected a $15,000 offer for his single-family home on 2024-11-08, preferring rental income; and invested $10,000 in a Turkish REIT on 2024-11-05. These recorded actions do not establish that later prospective property purchases were completed.

People recurring in James Perez’s real-estate and investment discussions: Amanda is his mentor and offered strategic guidance; Manuel is a fellow investor who shared property-management and REIT insights and recommended a REIT; Selin Kaya was considered as property manager, and agreed to an 8% management fee for a prospective third property on 2025-01-15; Mehmet Yilmaz was described by the assistant as a local real-estate agent; lawyer Mehmet was consulted or expected to review property contracts; Cem completed renovation punch-list items on 2024-11-03; Ayse Demir was associated with a planned property inspection on 2025-01-22; Randy joined James in a 2024 investment-return discussion.
rollups.topic: people in investment and property matters

rollups.text: James Perez’s recorded and planned property upkeep: he planned annual maintenance, insurance checks, year-end records, and tenant check-ins around 2024-11-10; Cem completed the renovation punch list on 2024-11-03; winterization was planned for 2024-11-15 and was later reported completed on 2024-12-13, two days before its reported 2024-12-15 scheduled date, at the Atatürk Street and Yenişehir properties. The reported winterization included pipe insulation, sealing gaps, and heating-system checks. Follow-up inspections were mentioned without dates.

Places James Perez visited or discussed for real-estate activity: he met Manuel at the North Ericshire Investors Meetup on 2024-03-05; took a three-day vacation to Cappadocia from 2024-11-02 through 2024-11-04; discussed investments in North Ericshire, Yenişehir, Atatürk Street, Cumhuriyet Avenue, and areas near transport links. The latter are investment locations discussed, not all confirmed visits.

James Perez’s Turkish REIT thread: he considered a $10,000 Turkish REIT investment on 2024-11-10, but the record states he had already invested $10,000 on 2024-11-05. On 2024-11-10 he found dividends and professional management appealing while worrying about Turkish economic and currency risks; he planned research and possibly financial-adviser consultation, and said he would monitor performance and fit with his strategy. He later described a 60/40 target split between direct property and REITs as reasonable, but no completed portfolio reallocation is recorded. Elapsed time from investment to the latest recorded discussion was five days.
rollups.topic: Turkish REIT investment and portfolio role

rollups.text: James Perez’s rental-property cash-flow and emergency-fund thread: on 2024-11-10 he discussed a three-day delayed tenant move-in that caused $350 of lost potential rent. A calculation using $620 scheduled rent and $824 monthly expenses estimated a $554 shortfall for the affected month. James said he would use his emergency fund and reduce non-essential spending; he planned to explain the delay, offer a $50 first-month rent discount, coordinate delivery, document the concession, and prepare better logistics and buffer time for future move-ins. The tenant move-in was scheduled for 2024-11-12; records do not confirm all planned actions or the fund’s balance. Key steps occurred within two days.
rollups.topic: delayed tenant move-in and cash-flow response

rollups.text: James Perez’s property-acquisition deliberations in January 2025: he assessed a $95,000 Cumhuriyet Avenue home advertised at 7% yield and planned a viewing, inspection, and offer process; on 2025-01-15 he said he wanted to add it and had allocated $55,000 for down payment and renovations, with a goal to close by 2025-03-01. The assistant proposed $19,000 down and $36,000 renovation allocation, among other uncompleted steps. In separate exchanges on 2025-01-15, James said he would proceed with a $120,000 North Ericshire duplex because of estimated positive cash flow, then said he chose the Cumhuriyet Avenue property over that duplex. The record does not resolve which plan he ultimately pursued or confirm any purchase. The stated March 1 closing goal was 45 days after January 15.
rollups.topic: property acquisition decisions and changing plans

rollups.text: James Perez’s conditional refinancing goal: on 2024-11-10 he discussed reviewing an exit plan and refinancing an investment-property mortgage after two years if the property appreciated 12%. The two-year point is 2026-11-10. He planned to track values and market trends, arrange appraisals, maintain a high credit score, and gather refinancing documents; no refinancing decision or completion is recorded. Elapsed time from the stated goal date to its conditional target is two years.

James Perez’s recorded property-insurance premium is $1,550 per year for Allianz policies covering both of his properties. The premium is mentioned in at least two records; the actual coverage allocation was not established.

James Perez’s rental-property winterization had one reported completion episode: work at the Atatürk Street and Yenişehir properties was completed on 2024-12-13, two days before the reported scheduled date of 2024-12-15. The work included pipe insulation, gap sealing, and heating-system checks.

James Perez’s property-management fee for Selin Kaya changed from a 10% fee discussed for the Yenişehir property in 2024 to an 8% fee that Selin agreed to charge for managing a prospective third property on 2025-01-15. The records do not establish that the fee change applied to the same property or the same management agreement; the 8% agreement’s included services were not confirmed.

James Perez’s stated real-estate allocation preferences evolved across discussions: he favored secure, methodical investing and steady rental income; on 2024-11-10 he leaned toward multifamily properties for income and scalability while also watching for appreciating single-family homes, and found a 60/40 direct-property/REIT target reasonable. On 2025-01-15 he agreed with prioritizing cash flow over property size, while also seeking both rental income and long-term appreciation. These are preferences and intentions, not confirmed portfolio allocations or completed purchases.

Cumhuriyet Avenue property purchase: On 2025-01-15, James Perez discussed evaluating the property, including yield, appreciation, due diligence, zoning, fire safety, and financing; many figures in these discussions were hypothetical. On 2025-01-18, an assistant-proposed timeline said to order title and zoning checks, but the conversation does not establish that this happened. On 2025-03-05, Mehmet confirmed the seller had accepted James’s $92,000 offer. On 2025-03-10, James decided to revise the offer to $90,000 and ask the seller to cover $2,000 in closing costs; although he approved a draft email, the draft reversed who would pay those costs, and sending it was not confirmed. Closing was scheduled for 2025-03-28 at 11:00 AM at North Ericshire Notary Office. From the accepted offer to the scheduled closing was 23 days; the revision came 5 days after the acceptance. The records do not confirm that closing occurred.

Cumhuriyet Avenue renovation: On 2025-03-10, James Perez planned a $2,500 renovation, prioritizing kitchen and bathroom improvements, paint, and landscaping; he later said he had secured a $2,300 cost with contractor Cem while wanting to preserve quality. The renovation was initially planned to start 2025-04-01, but a two-day materials-delivery delay moved the expected start to 2025-04-03. A separate later record says Cem was scheduled to start 2025-04-01 for an estimated three-week project, through 2025-04-21; the records therefore contain conflicting start expectations. On 2025-03-10, James worried the delay could jeopardize a 2025-03-22 completion deadline and tenant readiness, although the planned renovation start was after that deadline. He reported persistent supplier delays and asked about updates and notifications; no supplier contact channel, tenant notification, or title-company notification was confirmed. The delay was raised 24 days before the initially planned start, and the revised start was 2 days later than planned.

Property-management approach: James Perez said on 2025-03-10 that he had decided to self-manage and was focusing on it for now, valuing savings, learning, and personal control while worrying about time and the learning curve. He also preferred hands-on management for smaller properties and explored selectively outsourcing tasks or getting occasional professional advice; these explorations do not establish a final hybrid arrangement. Selin agreed to pause management services starting 2025-03-30, with no end date stated. James reported that Selin usually provided updates but sometimes required follow-up, especially off-hours. On 2025-03-10, James agreed to try weekly summary emails and considered a shared digital platform, with a follow-up meeting in a month viewed as useful but not confirmed scheduled. The records show a shift toward self-management alongside ongoing consideration of professional support, not a confirmed resumption of Selin’s services.

Susan and property visits: On 2025-01-13, Susan asked James Perez to limit property visits to weekends; on 2025-01-15, James worried about balancing that request with his investment strategy. On 2025-03-10, James said he would instead limit visits to weekdays before 6 PM, keep Susan updated about schedule changes and emergencies, batch tasks, and communicate schedules in advance. He also agreed to send Susan weekly summaries of visits, tasks, issues, and plans, and to notify her immediately about emergencies. The records do not explain the change from the earlier weekend-only request or establish Susan’s relationship to James. The arrangements were discussed over 56 days, from the initial request to the later stated plan.

Mortgage pre-approval and purchase deadlines: On 2025-01-15, James Perez was recorded as having applied to Halkbank for $45,000 mortgage pre-approval and seeking approval by 2025-01-25; he was concerned about missing documents and an extension that had not been granted. The assistant estimated 7–10 business days if the application was complete and uncomplicated. A separate record says James had a lawyer meeting scheduled for 2025-02-05 to review a purchase contract. Later guidance treated 2025-03-15 as the closing deadline and recommended completing legal review by February 5 and financing steps in time; February 10 was introduced by the assistant as a decision/pre-approval deadline, not established contract terms. The records do not confirm approval, an extension, or completion of the suggested steps. The stated pre-approval target preceded the scheduled lawyer meeting by 11 days.

Offer and renovation amounts changed or were clarified in the Cumhuriyet Avenue discussions: Mehmet confirmed acceptance of a $92,000 offer on 2025-03-05; on 2025-03-10 James decided to revise the offer to $90,000 and request $2,000 toward closing costs. Separately, James planned a $2,500 renovation budget and later reported securing a $2,300 renovation cost with Cem. These are distinct amounts and events; the records do not confirm the revised offer was sent or accepted.
rollups.topic: purchase offer and renovation budget changes

rollups.text: James Perez’s identified properties and property-related locations: Ataturk Street property (five-year hold considered May 20, 2025; zoning impacts discussed May 20, 2025); Cumhuriyet Avenue property (renovations completed May 12, 2025, tenant moved in May 15, 2025, and summer planting considered May 20, 2025); Yeni Mahalle single-family home (included in June 9, 2024 inspection summary); and North Ericshire, Turkey (James Perez’s stated residence and real-estate market of interest, date unspecified).

Safety inspections and outcomes discussed for James Perez’s properties: inspections on June 9, 2024 reportedly passed without violations at the Ataturk Street single-family home, Cumhuriyet Avenue multifamily property, and Yeni Mahalle single-family home; a pre-tenant inspection for a new property was reported completed April 19, 2025, but compliance was not verified; another safety inspection was scheduled for June 10, 2025, with no confirmed outcome in the records. James Perez wants prompt inspection results and explicit confirmation of inspection completion and compliance when assessing move-in readiness.

James Perez’s reported real-estate portfolio measures and targets: projected 2025 portfolio value of $180,000 (March 10, 2025); $3,200 monthly net cash flow (May 20, 2025); portfolio growth of 7.3% during Q1 2025, found with Randy (May 20, 2025); and year-to-date return of 7.2% against an initial 7% target (May 20, 2025). These figures refer to different measures and periods.

James Perez’s recurring wellness practices and stress concerns: he said daily meditation and weekly yoga were helpful and that he had been doing both by May 20, 2025; he also reported stress about reviewing his Q1 financials and concern about investment decisions affecting his mental health. In March 2025 he reported stress ahead of a scheduled March 20–22 retreat at Uludağ National Park. Suggested routines and coping methods were advice, not confirmed actions.

Property-management approach and communication: James Perez values hands-on control, customization, saving management fees, and responding quickly, while recognizing the workload, compliance, and maintenance burden (March 10, 2025). He was weighing self-management against hiring Selin and considered selective outsourcing of repairs and accounting. Selin agreed to pause management services starting March 30, 2025; the pause’s duration is unknown. On March 10, James agreed to try weekly summary emails, considered a shared digital platform, and favored a follow-up meeting. On May 20 he again considered a hybrid approach, but no decision to resume services or hire a manager was recorded.

Cumhuriyet Avenue renovation and tenant move-in: renovations were completed May 12, 2025, and a new tenant moved in May 15, 2025. On May 20, James Perez asked how to coordinate a move-in like this one. Recommendations included checking renovations, cleaning, confirming utilities and access, preparing lease and deposit documents, conducting a walkthrough, providing maintenance contacts, and following up; the records do not confirm whether those suggested steps were completed.

Planned additional acquisition: James Perez planned to acquire one more property by December 2025, with a $150,000 budget, as a means of growing his portfolio (plan recorded May 20, 2025). He asked about timing, negotiation, and investment due diligence; no purchase or selected property is recorded. The budget and target date recur in records from May 20, 2025.

Refinancing goal: James Perez set a goal to refinance two properties by the end of 2026 to fund future acquisitions (May 20, 2025). He asked how to prepare; suggested steps included reviewing existing loans and market conditions, organizing financial documents, comparing lenders, arranging appraisals, and budgeting closing costs. A quarterly 2026 preparation timeline was proposed, but no lender, loan terms, or completed refinancing steps were confirmed.

Manuel’s commercial-property co-investment offer: Manuel invited James Perez to co-invest on May 18, 2025. James expressed concern about whether he should have accepted, sought due-diligence and risk guidance, and later said he had declined the offer. On May 20, he asked whether declining was the right call. No deal terms or investment by James were reported.

James Perez rejected a $20,000 buyout offer concerning his multifamily property on May 10, 2025. On May 20, he asked about the long-term income implications and the trade-offs between retaining rental income and taking a payout, including how a market downturn might affect the decision. No change to the rejection or acceptance was recorded.

Relationship boundaries and property discussions with Susan: Susan requested fewer weekend property discussions starting May 10, 2025, so she could relax and avoid work talk. On May 20, James Perez proposed Tuesday evening discussions, keeping weekends free, researching property managers for day-to-day tasks, involving Susan in choosing one, and checking whether the arrangement works. James agreed to look into managers and involve Susan; no manager or specific meeting time was established. Separate records say James agreed to relationship boundaries with Susan starting May 10, without specifying them.

Three distinct inspection-related episodes are recorded: properties reportedly passed safety inspections on June 9, 2024; James reported completion of a pre-tenant inspection on April 19, 2025, without verified compliance; and a safety inspection was scheduled for June 10, 2025, with no recorded outcome. These are three discussed inspection episodes, not a confirmed count of all inspections ever performed.

James Perez reported an initial portfolio growth target of 7% and a year-to-date return of 7.2% on May 20, 2025, while a separate Q1 2025 review with Randy found 7.3% portfolio growth. These are two reported performance figures from distinct contexts; the records do not establish that they use the same calculation or period.

James Perez’s stated next-acquisition budget was consistently $150,000, with a target to acquire one additional property by December 2025. The budget and timing recur across multiple May 20, 2025 records; no acquisition completion is recorded.

James Perez’s recorded position on commercial property became explicit over the May 2025 discussions: he said he preferred residential properties, considered Manuel’s commercial co-investment invitation, and ultimately reported that he declined it on May 20, 2025. The records do not show a later change of mind or a commercial investment.
rollups.topic: residential preference and commercial offer decision
